name: Graneet
tagline: French ERP-lite for construction firms: quotes, progress billing, site cost tracking and invoicing in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible surface is quotes and invoices, which any agent can draft in an afternoon. The actual product is French construction billing: situations de travaux, avenants, retenue de garantie, autoliquidation de TVA, DGD, plus an invoicing trail that has to satisfy the anti-fraud rules and the e-invoicing mandate through a certified platform. Behind that sit accounting exports your comptable will actually accept and cost tracking tied to real purchase orders and subcontractors. A personal clone gets you pretty PDFs and a spreadsheet you trust less than the spreadsheet you already had. This is also not a personal-use category: nobody replaces a construction ERP for themselves on a Saturday.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that builds line-item quotes by lot, converts them into progress invoices with percentage-complete per line, and prints numbered PDFs.
requirements: A headless Chromium for PDF rendering
Your own VAT rates, legal mentions and numbering rules typed in by hand
An accountant willing to look at your CSV export
whatYouLose: Certified, mandate-compliant electronic invoicing and the audit trail that goes with it
Accounting exports your comptable accepts without complaining
Construction-specific billing mechanics done right: retenue de garantie, avenants, DGD, autoliquidation
Multi-user site cost tracking across purchase orders, suppliers and subcontractors
Support from people who know French BTP paperwork better than you do
moatNotes: French invoicing rules are a moving target with a legal deadline attached, which is exactly the kind of maintenance nobody wants to own personally.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the invoice is the product. A construction firm's cash flow runs on situations that clients accept and an accountant who can close the books, and both of those depend on paperwork that matches rules you did not write and cannot ignore. Paying a few hundred euros a month to never think about retenue de garantie formatting or the e-invoicing mandate is an obviously good trade for a business doing six or seven figures of work. The clone is only interesting as a learning exercise or as a quoting scratchpad.
notes: You can clone the quote builder in a weekend and it will look convincing right up until an accountant sees it. The moat is French construction billing law plus certified e-invoicing, and the fact that getting it wrong costs real money.
prompt:
Build a local-only quoting and progress-billing tool for a small construction business. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, server actions, no client state library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, migrations as plain .sql files run on boot
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- PDF generation by rendering a /print route and printing it with Playwright's Chromium to ./exports

Data model:
- client: name, address, siret, contact
- project: client, name, address, start date
- quote: project, number, status (draft, sent, accepted), vat rate per line
- lot: a named section inside a quote, ordered
- line: lot, description, unit (m2, ml, u, forfait, h), quantity, unit price, vat rate, computed total
- invoice: project, type (acompte, situation, solde), number, date, period, and per-line percentage complete
- payment: invoice, date, amount

Behaviour:
- Quote editor: add lots, add lines, reorder, live totals HT, TVA by rate, TTC
- Convert an accepted quote into a project with a billing schedule
- Create a situation: for each line enter cumulative percent complete, the app computes the amount for this period as cumulative minus previously invoiced, and refuses to go above 100 percent
- Apply a configurable retenue de garantie percentage withheld on each situation and show the running withheld balance
- Sequential, gapless invoice numbering per year, stored and never reused
- Legal mentions block editable in settings and injected into every PDF
- Dashboard: per project, quoted total, invoiced to date, paid to date, outstanding
- CSV export of invoices and lines in a flat accounting-friendly shape

Explicitly out of scope, say so in the README:
- No certified or legally compliant electronic invoicing, no Factur-X, no PDP transmission
- No autoliquidation handling, no multi-user, no supplier or subcontractor cost tracking
- No accounting software integration

Seed the database with one client, one project and a two-lot quote so the app is clickable immediately. Put the company identity in .env. Write a README that states plainly this is a personal tool and not a compliant invoicing system.
